findings.bug: The public validate/compile/preview/render loader still calls os.ReadFile and DetectKind on the entire root input before the bounded project loader runs. Thus the round-one bounded-read repair does not bound the public entry point. Neither path requires a regular input file. A CLI probe with a 32 MiB whitespace-padded manifest returned LIM_FILE_BYTES only after reaching 37,760 KiB peak RSS; a FIFO root input remained blocked until the probe killed it after one second.
findings.predicted: An oversized agent-authored or supplied manifest can exhaust CLI memory before receiving its documented size diagnostic, and a special-file input can hang before any Blender timeout or cancellation context exists. These scenarios need no concurrent hostile filesystem replacement.
findings.fix_hint: Use one regular-file, size-bounded root-input read before DetectKind, then pass the same snapshot into project resolution; reject nonregular module inputs as well.

findings.bug: Execution still uses exec.Cmd.CombinedOutput with no output cap in both the render launcher and version probe. The repair explicitly acknowledges in-memory logs, but the roadmap requires bounded logs; no bound or truncation path exists. Run also copies the captured bytes into Result.Stdout and formatted errors.
findings.predicted: A noisy or malfunctioning Blender run can consume arbitrary orchestrator memory during the five-minute job window, potentially terminating the CLI before it can persist its failed manifest. A timeout limits elapsed time, not bytes produced.
findings.fix_hint: Replace CombinedOutput with a capped log sink that drains both streams while retaining a bounded diagnostic tail and explicit truncation metadata; use it for Doctor too.
